assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a clear mechanistic arc from peptide identification and insulinotropic action to approved drugs with large, reproducible clinical benefit. Impact on the field and on patients is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 secretion and physiology), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology, GLP-2, translational link) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 form) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's drug-development role (liraglutide, semaglutide) is real but industrial, and Habener is not on the list, so credit allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large independent outcome trials, years of clinical use and a strong, stable mechanistic picture. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority disputes around Mojsov versus other early GLP-1 groups are not resolved here.
Whether the prize should reward physiology, drug design, or both is an open question.
I have not independently verified the details of the historical credit claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a genuinely new, general method to control defined cell populations with light and has changed neuroscience experimentation across systems, circuits and disease models. Discovery of channelrhodopsin plus its adaptation to neurons forms a clear, original, lasting contribution.
assessment.attribution: A compound discovery: microbial rhodopsin channel discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and neuronal implementation (Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenboeck) are separate steps. A three-person split must leave out several key contributors. I propose Deisseroth for the neuronal toolbox and Hegemann and Nagel for channelrhodopsin function, accepting that Bamberg and Boyden are omitted.
assessment.maturity: Mature in tools and basic research, with enormous independent adoption. Clinical translation is still early but the prize concerns the method.
uncertainties: Six credited names cannot all be honoured; the optimal three is genuinely contested.
Relative weight of the discovery of channelrhodopsin versus its use in neurons is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against tumour antigens have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new therapeutic modality. The discovery is clear and has changed the field of cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28-costimulated CARs), June (4-1BB CARs and clinical translation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, early gene-engineered T cells) are a defensible trio. Eshhar, Kuwana, Finney, and others are not on the supplied list, so the allocation is incomplete and possibly contested.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: several approved products and long follow-up in lymphoma and leukaemia. Solid-tumour efficacy and long-term safety remain limited.
uncertainties: Missing foundational contributors such as the earliest chimeric receptor work are not credited in the supplied list.
Long-term toxicity and applicability beyond haematological cancers are unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed by innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer. It is a compact, original mechanism with broad conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, which is the decisive step; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING. I propose Chen, Barber and Ishikawa, leaving out Sun and Wu as contributors to the cGAS identification in Chen's lab.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and rapidly expanding, though therapeutic translation (agonists, inhibitors) is not yet established clinically, so recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether Chen and Barber need to be joined by another STING contributor is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that blocking TNF alleviates rheumatoid arthritis introduced anti-cytokine therapy for chronic inflammatory disease and led to a broadly used drug class. Both the concept and the clinical impact are clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini form a compact, well-defined duo that links the cytokine-cascade concept in synovial cells to the clinical trials. Contributions of others (for instance the antibody developers) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: decades of use, confirmation across multiple indications and biosimilars. Recognition is long established and not premature.
uncertainties: The question of whether the prize should include the people who generated the TNF biology and the antibodies is open.
I have not independently verified the allocation of credit among clinical and laboratory contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL in chronic myeloid leukaemia proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and changed a fatal disease into a manageable one. Clinical and conceptual impact is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical translation and the case for the ABL inhibitor) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. The upstream discovery of BCR-ABL itself lies outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: over two decades of clinical use, with durable responses and well-characterised resistance. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Relation to the BCR-ABL fusion discovery and the Philadelphia chromosome, which are not credited here, may complicate a prize.
The relative importance of industrial and clinical contributions is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides for SMN2 yielded nusinersen, a clear mechanism-to-therapy success that changed outcomes in spinal muscular atrophy and validated antisense splicing modulation as a platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and identifying the target) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) are a coherent duo. Others in the SMN2 antisense story (for example Hua, Singh) are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for a therapy: approved since 2016 with growing real-world data. Overall the field is still developing, so recognition could be a little early.
uncertainties: Competing SMA therapies (gene replacement, small molecule) may affect how the prize is framed.
Long-term durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-lived adult-stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5-positive cells created a widely used experimental system for tissue biology and disease modelling. The advance is original and has had broad impact on stem-cell and cancer research.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the work on Lgr5 stem cells and organoid culture, and Sato performed the key culture work. This duo looks fair, though earlier work by others on three-dimensional culture is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and confirmed independently, but medical applications are still maturing, so impact on patient treatment is yet limited.
uncertainties: Overlap with pluripotent-stem-cell-derived organoid work and earlier 3D culture is not captured here.
